Uber — peer benchmark

UBER-peer-benchmark-2026-10-14 · USD · series 2026-10-14T02:30:00Z · built 2026-10-14 03:15 UTC

The short version

Riders and eaters pay Uber to get a car or a meal to their door, and merchants and drivers pay it to reach them. Lyft, DoorDash, and Grab sell the same two jobs, rides and delivery, in different places and in different mixes. Lyft is Uber's direct US and Canada ride-hailing rival, with no delivery business. DoorDash is the US delivery leader against Uber Eats, with no rides. Grab runs rides and delivery together across Southeast Asia, the closest copy of Uber's two-sided model outside its main markets. All four report in US dollars, so they sit on one axis without conversion.

Operating income is the profit line every name prints. Margin is that line divided by the company's own revenue.

Lyft's multiple is blank today: its fourth-quarter EPS is not printed, so no trailing four quarters can be summed. Its roughly 2× in early 2026 reflected a one-time tax benefit in FY2025 earnings, not operating profit.

Key metrics

MetricTrendLine
RevenueLargest by farUber's 2025 revenue of $52.0B is almost four times DoorDash ($13.7B), eight times Lyft ($6.3B), and fifteen times Grab ($3.4B).
Operating incomeOnly large, steady profitUber earned $5.6B of operating income in 2025; DoorDash $0.7B, Grab $0.07B, Lyft a $0.2B loss.
Operating marginHighest in the setUber 13.3% in Q2 2026 against DoorDash 3.5% and Lyft 2.6%.
Trailing multiple (2026-W41)Lowest with a figureUber 15.4×; Grab 52×; DoorDash 101×; Lyft blank (no printed fourth-quarter EPS).
Diluted share countShrinking at UberUber's diluted shares fell from 2.15B in 2024 to 2.05B in Q2 2026; DoorDash is flat; Lyft is lower.
Diluted EPS growthStrong latest quarterUber's Q2 2026 diluted EPS rose 86% year over year, against Lyft up 30% and DoorDash down 29%.

Open gaps

  • Lyft's fourth-quarter diluted EPS and share counts are blank: neither its annual report nor its fourth-quarter earnings release prints a three-month per-share line, and we do not take the year less nine months.
  • Grab's diluted share counts for the first three quarters of 2021 are blank: those releases print no prior-year share count.
  • Quarters before each listing are blank (Lyft before 2018, DoorDash before 2020, Grab before 2021), as are Lyft's 2017–2018 and DoorDash's 2018 per-share figures.
  • Grab's 2019–2022 share count is the single "basic and diluted" figure its annual report prints.
  • Uber's 2017–2019 figures are as first filed in its 2019 annual report, read by this page (DERIVED); Grab's quarters are read from its earnings releases (DERIVED).
  • Weekly multiples are blank wherever trailing earnings were a loss; year-over-year growth is blank wherever the prior period was a loss or the sign flipped, as named in each chart.
  • Take rate, trips, orders and gross bookings are not on this page: Uber, Lyft, DoorDash and Grab each define them differently.
  • Forward multiples are empty for every name.
